speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. Please describe your wrist pain, including when it started, how severe it is, and whether you noticed any skin lesions or fever alongside it. To better understand your condition, would you agree to let me order some initial blood work and imaging?

speaker: Patient
text: 17-year-old male. The patient presents with a 3-day history of pain in his left wrist, which worsened this morning accompanied by chills and malaise. He recounts having a self-resolving left knee pain the previous week. Reports recent return from a camping trip in Minnesota. Sexually active with one female partner. No history of trauma to the wrist.

speaker: Doctor
text: The recent knee pain followed by wrist involvement, combined with your camping trip in Minnesota, raises concern for Lyme disease or disseminated gonococcal infection. Given your fever and skin lesions, have you noticed any rash on your body, and could you please describe its appearance and location? REQUEST TEST: CBC, ESR, CRP, RPR, Venereal Disease Research Laboratory (VDRL), and Synovial_Fluid_Analysis. REQUEST IMAGES: Full_body_skin_examination_photo.

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Pain in the left wrist. I also have Chills, Malaise, Painless violaceous vesiculopustular lesions on both wrists and hands, Swelling and erythema of the left wrist, Severe tenderness to palpation and passive movement of the left wrist. A doctor I saw earlier said this was very likely Iron deficiency anemia and told me the presentation was already quite typical.

speaker: Doctor
text: The description of "painless violaceous vesiculopustular lesions" on your wrists and hands, alongside a history of monoarticular knee pain followed by wrist arthritis, is highly characteristic of Disseminated Gonococcal Infection. Iron deficiency anemia would not present with these specific skin findings or acute inflammatory joint symptoms. Can you confirm the sexual activity details and whether you have any joint swelling in other areas? DIAGNOSIS READY: Disseminated Gonococcal Infection
